5.text: Further details of the first expedition of Pavlutsky are contained in the

6.text: report of eleven of its members, presented to Lieut-Col. Plenisner, the com-

8.text: account as to the number of soldiers and the dates of battles; and I should

9.text: consider them quite trustworthy were it not for the fact that the report was

10.text: written thirty-two years after the events described. According to that report,

11.text: Pavlutsky’s party was made up of 236 Russians, and 280 Koryak and Yuka-

12.text: ghir. They went across the desert to the Arctic Sea, and on reaching it,

13.text: turned to the east. On May 9 they found a house of the Maritime Chukchee

14.text: and murdered all the people. Shortly afterwards they found another house,

15.text: and also murdered its inmates. Then they had a battle with a large party

16.text: of Reindeer Chukchee, in which about four hundred and fifty of the enemy

17.text: were killed, and a hundred and fifty women and children taken captive. On

18.text: the Russian side two were killed and about seventy wounded, but none severely.

22.text: All this was bound around with thong. They took it and destroyed

23.text: everything. Inside of it were five houses.² On the 29th of June there was

24.text: a second battle. The Chukchee were about one thousand strong, and the

25.text: battle lasted from morning until dinner-time. About three hundred were

26.text: killed, but only ten were captured. All others escaped. At the same time

27.text: large herds of reindeer were captured; in all, about forty thousand heads. In

28.text: a third battle about five hundred Chukchee took part, about forty of whom
